title: Rinny Rahmania
text:
Brief introduction

I’m from Indonesia - the largest archipelagics state in equator, comprised of thousands of islands and a vast coastal areas. There are many emerging issues are occurred in marine and coastal areas here, remain unsolved. And these challenges offer opportunities to develop some useful tools or even create innovations that can be tested here, then applied in other coastal areas across the globe.

I lead the Research Group for Coastal Ecological Modelling in Indonesia, who focusing our research field on Remote Sensing, GIS, Blue Carbon, Coastal Ecology, Coastal Spatial Planning, Sustainable Coastal Cities, and Marine Debris.

title: Rinny Rahmania
text:
About me

 Field of expertise


Remote sensing application, blue carbon, marine and coastal resources management, coastal spatial planning, marine debris


 Education



 Doctorate: Montpellier University (2016)


 Graduate: IPB University (2005)


 Undergraduate: Haluoleo University (2001)



 Work Experience




BRIN (The National Research and Innovation Agency), Indonesia | 2022 – Present




I am a senior researcher at Ecology Research center - BRIN, Indonesia; and lead the Coastal Modelling research group.





KKP (Ministry of Marine Affairs and Fisheries), Indonesia | 2006 – 2022




I started my career as researcher at Marine Technology Research Center - an institution under the Ministry of Marine Affairs and Fisheries at time.




 Accomplishments


I have obtained number of research grant from various institutions, i.e.: from World Bank, AFD (France), APEC, and from various Indonesian government agencies. You may find publications resulted from these funding at my researchgate page.


 Research interests


Remote Sensing and GIS application development, Blue Carbon, Coastal Ecology, Coastal Spatial Planning, Sustainable Coastal Cities, Marine Debris.

title: This is my personal page that the themes customized from Robert Michel’s
text:
I’ve been observing many examples before making my own github page. By far, Michell’s theme suits my purpose. Highly appreciate for showcasing this great work.


This page has three main sections:

blog
projects
lesson


Each has it’s own landing page and _metadata.yml file. Additionally the ejs directory contains a small custom listing template for the main landing page.
I agree with Michell’s idea that some older blog posts should not be rendered; rather, they’re sort of put together with images and text.
Lessons and projects use an <iframe> to source the html file in with an option to make it full screen, which I thought was a neat idea.




More settings and configuration for this theme, check the following resources: 1. Quarto documentation page (https://quarto.org/docs/websites/) 2. Robert Michell’s website (https://robertmitchellv.com/) and his repository (https://github.com/robertmitchellv/robertmitchellv.github.io)
